text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Fiat honorary chairman Giovanni Agnelli said politicians should stop "bothering" Bank of Italy governor about a possible cut in interest rates as a central bank head's main duty is that of complete independence. Agnelli also said he was confident Italy would join the first wave of European Economic and Monetary Union (all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi said he had never tried to interfere with Bank of Italy governor Fazio's stand on interest rates. Prodi, attending the Denver G7 summit, also stressed th importance of reforming the country's welfare state (all).

* In an interview, hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said centre-left government's document on reforms to the welfare state ought to be re-written as it was not approved by trade unions and by the hard left (La Repubblica).

* The Italian Treasury said it had fixed a maximum share price of 9,325 lire for the third tranche pubblic offer of energy giant ENI. The sale of the third tranche starts today, the final price for the shares will be based on the closing value on the Milan bourse of next Friday (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
